### NAME

`mcp-kali-server` - MCP Kali Server — Kali toolchain exposed over MCP for agent operators (third-party deliverable).

### SYNOPSIS & usage

*Derived from the upstream README at generation
time; verify against `--help` where the tool is
installed.*

```
sudo apt install mcp-kali-server
kali-server-mcp
```

```
git clone https://github.com/Wh0am123/MCP-Kali-Server.git
cd MCP-Kali-Server
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
./server.py
```

### DESCRIPTION (upstream)

**MCP Kali Server (MKS)** is a lightweight API bridge that connects [MCP clients](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/clients) (e.g: [Claude Desktop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop) or [5ire](https://github.com/nanbingxyz/5ire)) to the [API server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/examples) which allows executing commands on a Linux terminal. This MCP is able to run terminal commands as well as interacting with web applications using: - `Dirb` - `enum4linux` - `gobuster` - `Hydra` - `John the Ripper` - `Metasploit-Framework` - `Nikto` - `Nmap` - `sqlmap` - `WPScan` - As well as being able to execute raw commands. As a result, this is able to perform **AI-assisted penetration testing** an

### OPTIONS (upstream README)

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ip` | <address>`: Specify the IP address to bind the server to (default: `127.0.0.1` for localhost only) |
| `--port` | <port>`: Specify the port number (default: `5000`) |
| `--debug` | Enable debug mode for verbose logging |
